text:
hina: quick heads-up — int8 bring-up on open-llama-v2 (staging) shows a tokenization mismatch for mixed zh/jp names, plus a BLEU drop on long zh->en examples. dug in a bit, posting snippets and metrics below.

liam: can you paste the tokenized examples? is this before or after our detoken normalization?

hina: before detok-normalize. example: 
```
原来 李白という -> tokens: [原, 来,  李白, と, いう]
原来 李白 という -> tokens: [原来, 李, 白, という]
```
both come from same dataset entry depending on byte-level split. seems the int8 quantized tokenizer model variant produced extra merges in the Han+Kana boundary.

maya: metric summary? short sentences vs long?

hina: short (<30 tok) negligible diff. long (>=120 chars) drops: BLEU 29.3 -> 25.8, chrF 0.58 -> 0.53, rouge-l -1.9. Repro steps: run staging-int8 runner (profile A), eval harness zh->en newstest subset 2k examples, seed fixed.

liam: odd — tokenizer should be deterministic. Are we sure it's not an offline script using older tokenmap?

hina: checked hashes: tokenmap v2.4 used by base and int8, but the runtime kernel does a small pre-token merge for efficiency (batch prefix compaction). suspect compaction + mixed-script grapheme boundary bug.

raj: tagging platform: could this be an artifact of our batching window (256->64) change in the int8 runtime? it reduces KV alignment and might be changing prefix caching offsets.

hina: possible. I ran a micro-batch test with batching disabled and the token splits normalized back to expected behavior.

maya: can you attach a tiny failing pair so I can add to regression suite? I want to run an eval across all quant levels (fp16, q4, q8, int8) with same seed.

hina: pasted 3 minimal repros below (one mixed zh/jp name, one long news paragraph, one emoji+han edge-case).
```
1) 原来李白という人がここにいた。
2) 【长篇】去年，政府在多个城市展开了大规模的基础设施项目……（长段落省略）
3) 张三🙂さんは東京に来た。
```

eval-bot: queued job 654321 for maya: eval/full-run on open-llama-v2 variants (fp16,q4,q8,int8) — ETA ~42m.

liam: if this is compaction-related we should try: disable prefix compaction -> run int8 -> compare tokenization. If fixed, we can add a guarded flag for mixed-script sequences.

hina: agreed. I'll run compaction-off int8 job now on a 200-sample shard and post diffs.

maya: FYI also check rtl patterns — we've seen separate regressions where trailing punctuation gets attached to Arabic tokens after quantization. might be the same boundary logic.

hina: good call. adding an Arabic/Russian quick-check.

raj: if we confirm it's runtime-driven, plan: short-term revert compaction for mixed-script routes; medium-term: add grapheme-aware compaction and unit tests.

liam: assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml pairing. thanks — keep thread updated. :thumbsup:

hina: will do. posting results in ~15m for the 200-sample run.
